title: Possibility 1.6
statement_text: For all $c > 0$, there exists $\xi > 0$ with the following property. For every graph $H$ with congestion at most $\xi$, there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for every graph $G$ with $|G| > 1$ that is $H$-free and $\bar{H}$-free, there is a pure pair $A, B$ in $G$ with $|A| \geq \varepsilon|G|$ and $|B| \geq \varepsilon|G|^{1-c}$.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple, $|G|$ is the number of vertices, $\bar H$ is the complement of $H$, and $G$ is $H$-free if no induced subgraph of $G$ is isomorphic to $H$. A pure pair in $G$ is a pair $A,B$ of disjoint vertex sets that are complete (all edges between them present) or anticomplete (no edges). The congestion of a graph $H$ with at least one edge is the maximum of $1-(|J|-1)/|E(J)|$ over all subgraphs $J$ of $H$ with at least one edge (and $0$ if $H$ has no edge); it is $0$ iff $H$ is a forest, and small congestion means roughly large girth and maximum average degree only slightly above $2$. By Erdős, Hajnal and Pach, for every $H$ there are $\varepsilon,b>0$ such that every $H$-free and $\bar H$-free $G$ has a pure pair with both sides of size at least $\varepsilon|G|^b$, and the authors ask when $b$ can be close to $1$. Their main theorem: if $c>0$ and one of $H,\bar H$ has congestion at most $c/(9+15c)$, then there is $\varepsilon>0$ such that every $H$-free and $\bar H$-free graph $G$ with $|G|>1$ has a pure pair with $|A|,|B|\ge\varepsilon|G|^{1-c}$; conversely, if both $H$ and $\bar H$ have congestion more than $c$, no such $\varepsilon$ exists. For forests $H$ (congestion $0$) both sides can be linear (Chudnovsky, Scott, Seymour, Spirkl), and in an earlier paper they showed that for $H$ of branch-length at least $4c^{-1}+5$ one side can be linear and the other of size $\varepsilon|G|^{1-c}$. This "possibility" asks whether the same strengthening (one side linear) holds under small congestion; the authors were unable to decide it. Their proof does not give it because one step must shrink the blocks of the structure by factors polynomial in $|G|$ rather than by constant factors.

title: Open question on Theorem 3.3 with stronger coherence
statement_text: Let $\beta\ge2$ be an integer, let $H$ be a $\beta$-buildable graph, and let $c>1/\lfloor(\beta-3)/3\rfloor$. Is it true that there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that every $\varepsilon$-sparse $(\varepsilon|G|^{1-c},\varepsilon|G|)$-coherent graph $G$ with $|G|>1$ contains $H$ (as an induced subgraph)?
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple, $|G|$ is the number of vertices, $\bar H$ is the complement of $H$, and $G$ is $H$-free if no induced subgraph of $G$ is isomorphic to $H$. A pure pair in $G$ is a pair $A,B$ of disjoint vertex sets that are complete (all edges between them present) or anticomplete (no edges). The congestion of a graph $H$ with at least one edge is the maximum of $1-(|J|-1)/|E(J)|$ over all subgraphs $J$ of $H$ with at least one edge (and $0$ if $H$ has no edge); it is $0$ iff $H$ is a forest, and small congestion means roughly large girth and maximum average degree only slightly above $2$. A graph $G$ is $\varepsilon$-sparse if every vertex has degree less than $\varepsilon|G|$, and $(\gamma,\delta)$-coherent if there is no anticomplete pair $A,B$ with $|A|\ge\gamma$ and $|B|\ge\delta$. Adding a handle to a graph means adding an induced path $P$ of length at least two between two existing vertices, whose internal vertices are new and have degree two. $H$ is $\beta$-buildable if it can be built from a two-vertex graph with no edges by repeatedly adding handles of length at least $\beta$; graphs of small congestion are induced subgraphs of such graphs. The authors prove the statement with the hypothesis $(\varepsilon|G|^{1-c},\varepsilon|G|^{1-c})$-coherent; since every such graph is also $(\varepsilon|G|^{1-c},\varepsilon|G|)$-coherent, the question asks whether a weaker hypothesis suffices. This proven version is the sparse core of their main theorem: if one of $H,\bar H$ has congestion at most $c/(9+15c)$, every $H$-free and $\bar H$-free graph has a pure pair with both sides of size at least $\varepsilon|G|^{1-c}$. The weaker coherence hypothesis suffices for almost all of their proof, and an affirmative answer would be a step towards the possibility that one side of the pure pair can be taken linear.
